summary: Batched long-context requests intermittently abort with 503/stream disconnects when max_tokens high
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when sending batched generation requests that include very large context prefixes (200k+ tokens) and high max_tokens (40k+), about 5-15% of requests in the batch terminate with an HTTP 503 or the streaming connection aborts mid-generation. Failures typically happen between 35s-75s after request start and often occur on the finalization step (flush/final chunk).

Impact:
- NovusHealth feeds multi-document patient histories as a single prompt; intermittent generation aborts result in missing critical notes in downstream processing.
- Customer reports increased retry churn and billing variance for partial responses.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity; prod - us-east.
- Requests are client-batched (client sends 8 concurrent requests in a single connection) with keep-alive and streaming responses enabled.
- Observed across two model families (gpt4o-redwood-70b and llama-2-70b-bleeding).

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Build prompt by concatenating ~250k tokens from clinical notes.
2) Call /v1/generate with max_tokens=45000, stream=true.
3) Use client-side batching: 6-10 requests in parallel on the same connection.
4) Observe that some requests return 503 or stream terminates with "upstream reset" while others complete.

Logs (examples):
- gateway: "upstream returned 503: handler timeout after 58.206s for request SUP-88219-customer-call"
- runtime: "evicting KV cache entry due to memory pressure, evicted 3 segments for model gpt4o-redwood-70b, request_id=abc123"
- scheduler: "batch overcommit: requested_budget=52000, allocated=48000 -> delaying finalization"

Additional notes:
- Customer attached request IDs and timestamps to the ticket and allowed SRE access to trace logs.
- Customer states reducing max_tokens to ~10k reduces error rate to <1% but is not acceptable for their workflow.

2026-03-12 16:02 - Connor Li (SRE): Confirmed reproducible on our internal dedicated cluster using their payload sample. Observed streaming resets on ~12% of batched requests with identical inputs when max_tokens > 30k.

2026-03-12 18:20 - Marina Gomez (Runtime eng): Noted recent change in batching heuristic (PR #3421) that allows packing by estimated remaining tokens; pushing to reproduce locally with and without the heuristic.

2026-03-12 22:05 - Connor Li (SRE): Reproduced locally. When heuristic enabled, batch controller sometimes groups requests that cause combined token budget to exceed node allocation leading to KV eviction and head-of-line blocking. Turning heuristic off eliminated 503s in test.

2026-03-13 09:12 - NovusHealth (Customer): Provided additional payloads and confirmed that temporarily reducing client concurrency is an acceptable short-term mitigation while a patch is developed. Thankful for timeline estimate.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis: recent batching heuristic (PR 3421) overestimates safe packing when prefixes are very large. This leads to batch overcommit where combined per-batch token budgets exceed node memory/KV cache thresholds -> triggers eviction during generation finalization -> some streaming connections abort with 503 or upstream reset.

Evidence: reproducer runs with heuristic ON show 10-15% failures; with heuristic OFF failures drop to <1%. Kernel traces show finalizer waiting on KV segments that were concurrently evicted and reloaded, creating stalls and timeouts.

Scheduler logs show 'batch overcommit' entries matching timestamps of customer failures. evict metrics spike during incidents. No evidence of network flakiness at gateway level beyond the 503s issued by upstream runner.

Risk assessment: issue primarily affects large-prefix + high max_tokens + client-side batching. Dedicated customers using smaller max_tokens or single-request patterns unaffected. However, regression was introduced in last 2 weeks and could impact other enterprise customers using large contexts.
Related tickets: SUP-84127 (kv eviction on large prefix), SUP-29541 (context tail latency) — similar symptoms but different root causes identified in earlier triage.
workaround:
- Ask customer to reduce client-side concurrency (recommended 1-2 concurrent requests) or reduce max_tokens to <= 10k until soft fix deployed.
- For Dedicated customers, increase node KV cache memory (if committed) or route these high-budget requests to a region/node with higher capacity.
- Disable the new batching heuristic by setting runtime flag 'enable_heuristic_pack=false' in dedicated cluster config (requires minor config restart).
resolution:
WIP - short-term: disabled packing heuristic on affected dedicated pool (rolled back to pre-PR3421 behavior) which reduced error rate to <1% in canary.
Planned long-term fix: update batch controller to account for absolute prefix size and add per-request token budget-estimation that factors KV segment count; also add backpressure at API gateway when estimated per-request finalization time exceeds threshold. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/3429.
Rollout notes: will roll to 10% of dedicated nodes first, monitor evict_count, finalizer latencies, and 5xx rates for 6 hours before expanding. Postmortem doc to be created at linked confluence page.
